lock_files.notes: Same flock(2) lease files as any-core.sh, both-cores.sh and pf-launch. Lock order: GPU files first (testing-gpu.lock, then testing-gpu-<UUID>.lock), then core leases. Owner job units take them for their lifetime (GPU files handed over by the queue's GPU claim when the GPU was contended); the worker itself only observes /proc/locks. Borrow jobs hold borrow-core<K>.lock shared instead, never the core lease; holding borrow-core<K>.lock exclusively from outside the queue marks core K as not lendable. 16 cores: core K's lease is testing-core<K>.lock for K = 0-5 and 7-15 (core 6: testing-core.lock), its borrow lease borrow-core<K>.lock.

borrow.notes: Borrow jobs (simq submit --borrow) run in simqborrow.slice, a top-level slice of the user manager with cpu.idle=1, as units with CPUWeight=1, SCHED_IDLE and idle I/O class: every owner job unit and every process of the terminal sessions wins the CPU. A lease holder or owner job is idle when its process tree used at most idle_threshold cores above a whole number over idle_window_s and the core itself was at most cpu_idle_threshold busy; a borrower lent such a core is preempted when the tree uses more than the cores left to it plus busy_threshold over busy_window_s. A frozen borrower is requeued after freeze_max_s or shortly before its time limit. backfill_waiting_owners (0.6.3): a free core that a waiting owner job needs is lent only to a borrow job whose time limit ends before that owner job can start (EASY backfill); without it such cores are not lent at all while the owner job waits, which in a single pool would hold every borrow job back whenever any owner job waits.

partitions.name: zenobia
partitions.description: zenobia: one pool of every physical core and the GPU (0.6.3: no partitions)

notes: 0.6.3: no partitions. One pool, zenobia, of the 16 physical cores (each named by its lowest logical CPU, 0-15) and the GPU; every job requests from it. Logical CPU numbering of the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2: physical cores 0-15 (first threads), SMT siblings 16-31 (never allocated). Install only on that CPU: the topology check reads sysfs and refuses this file on the 8-core CPU.

The partition names used before 0.6.3 (spheral, raikou-mfem, powerflow) are aliases of zenobia: -p spheral|raikou-mfem|powerflow keeps working, with the defaults those partitions had (cores, memory, time) and their old cores tried first (prefer_cpus); limits are the pool's. A job keeps the name it was submitted with (SIMQ_PARTITION, simq listings). Jobs recorded under these names before 0.6.3 are adopted and scheduled under zenobia.

Without -p a job goes to zenobia with the defaults of the old default partition (spheral): 4 cores, 18G, 2 days, lowest free cores first. Limits: 20G memory, 14 days (the largest of the old partitions).
memory_schedulable is the sum of --mem over concurrent jobs (31 GiB RAM; about 3 GiB left for the system).
The GPU is a scheduled resource of the pool: exclusive per job unless --gpu-mem is given and the 11G budget allows sharing; queued GPU jobs win the GPU lease files through the GPU line.

Lending: free cores and the idle cores of running owner jobs go to borrow jobs (lend: true). Cores leased by tools outside the queue (any-core.sh, both-cores.sh, pf-launch) are not lent (lend_leased_idle: false). Timing-sensitive runs submit with --exclusive-timing, which keeps the job's cores and their SMT siblings unlent while it runs.
No GPU is ever lent: borrow jobs cannot request GPUs.

gpu_line.notes: 0.6.2 GPU line. Queued GPU jobs that are ready except for the GPU join the line through a claim unit (<prefix>-gpuclaim-<token>.service) that waits for testing-gpu.lock in the kernel queue, then takes testing-gpu-<UUID>.lock, and hands both open files to the job unit (SCM_RIGHTS), so the lock is never released in between and the job's time limit starts with its unit. gpu-lease users publish tickets in ticket_dir; members are served by since-time (a claim's is the submit time of its oldest ready job, a helper's its start time). Processes blocked in a raw flock on the GPU files (command in requeue_commands, not a job-control job of an interactive shell) are moved behind the line with SIGSTOP+SIGCONT; every move is logged in log_path. state_path lists the waiting queue jobs with their since-times, the claim, the holders and the raw waiters (heartbeat every 10 s; stale after stale_after_s, withdrawn when the worker stops). A held claim that no job takes within claim_hold_max_s releases the GPU.
